content.title: Share State Deliberately
content.context:
```text
App
 └── Account
      └── AccountHeader
           └── AccountName
```

If only `AccountName` needs the account name, the value can travel through props.

```text
App
  ↓ props
Account
  ↓ props
AccountHeader
  ↓ props
AccountName
```

This is explicit. Anyone reading the tree can see the path.
goals: Choose between props and context based on how far data must travel and whether the relationship is truly shared.

content.title: When the path becomes noisy
content.text:
Now imagine the same value must pass through many layers that do not use it.

That can become repetitive.

React provides Context for information that needs to be available to many components deep in a tree without manually passing it through every intermediate component.

content.question: Which situation is the stronger reason to consider context?

options.text: Two components are siblings and one can simply pass a value to the other through their parent.
Many distant descendants need the same application-wide or subtree-wide information.
A single input has one local value.
A temporary animation flag exists in one component.

feedback.correct: Context is useful when information is broadly shared. It is not a replacement for all props.
feedback.incorrect: Context is useful when information is broadly shared. It is not a replacement for all props.

content.title: Context is a boundary, too
content.text:
Imagine:

```jsx
<ThemeContext.Provider value={theme}>
  <AppShell />
</ThemeContext.Provider>
```

The provider creates a boundary: components beneath it can read the shared value.

The important design question is not “Can I use context?”

It is:

**“Is this information truly shared enough to deserve this boundary?”**

content.question:
You have a `ProfileCard` with a `name` prop used only by the card.

Should the whole application move that name into context?

options.text: Yes, because context is always cleaner.
No. The prop is local to the relationship and is already explicit.
Yes, because props should never be used for data.
Only if the card is large.

feedback.correct: Context has a cost too: it hides some data flow. Prefer explicit props when the relationship is simple.
feedback.incorrect: Context has a cost too: it hides some data flow. Prefer explicit props when the relationship is simple.
